title: The REAL Reason I Quit YouTube (And Why I’m Back)
promo_conflict: Self-promotional: the host discusses his own businesses and promotes the channel's return and future videos; no paid sponsor is disclosed.

stated_problem.quote: So I'm staring at a YouTube channel that I no longer have a product for.
stated_problem.speaker: Host (name not stated)

idea.name: Niche Pursuits YouTube channel
idea.one_liner: Business education videos build an audience and have historically directed viewers toward the host's software products.
idea.offer: Business education videos and interaction with the creator and community.
idea.revenue_model: Historically, the channel built awareness for software sales through an email list and podcast; the host says the current video has no ads and no software funnel.

key_quotes.quote: So while I do genuinely enjoy creating videos for YouTube and interacting with the community that watches those videos, my main business reasons has always been to eventually sell more software.
First, I've discovered that I truly do enjoy the creative process.
Being able to connect with others and share in their business education and success makes me feel like my content is actually useful.

claims.quote: And somehow this channel crossed 100,000 subscribers.
